champion: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma
ordered_diagnoses: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic skin eruption with atypical lymphocytic infiltrate
salient_findings: Multiple erythematous and violaceous plaques and nodules on the buttocks
Atypical lymphocytic infiltrate in the dermis with eosinophils and plasma cells
key_facts: Male patient in his 70s
Eruption duration of 5 years
Previous treatments with oral antibiotics, oral doxepin, and UV-B phototherapy failed
History of HSV-2 infection on the buttocks
Syphilis screen results were negative
Molecular analysis of the T-cell receptor gamma gene showed a weak clonal band
Repeat molecular studies showed no evidence of clonal rearrangement
Biopsy findings of dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes
Epidermotropism identified in second biopsy
Eosinophils and plasma cells present in the dermal infiltrate
